decision: persistent coordinator wrapper around MissionQueue + MissionQueueStore
scope: lab orchestration and synthetic worker reliability
winner: serialized coordinator wrapper with fail-closed persistence

comparison.approach: serialized coordinator wrapper with fail-closed persistence
comparison.correctness: high: every queue mutation is serialized and acknowledged only after atomic snapshot save
comparison.robustness: high for single-process coordinator restart and concurrent callers; storage failure poisons the coordinator instead of continuing with false durability
comparison.latency: moderate: one whole-snapshot write per mutation
comparison.resourceUse: low at current lab scale; no external service
comparison.regressionRisk: low: leaves MissionQueue semantics unchanged and composes the tested store
comparison.qa: restart recovery, idempotency, concurrent mutation serialization, and persistence-failure fail-closed tests

whyItWon: It closes the current orchestration persistence gap with the smallest change surface. Queue behavior remains independently testable, writes are serialized, restart recovery is explicit, and a failed store cannot silently leave the coordinator operating as if state were durable.
failuresAndLessons: Atomic rename protects against partial snapshot replacement but whole-state snapshots remain O(n) per mutation.
Fail-closed persistence prevents further mutation after a write failure, but production recovery still needs an operator restart/reconciliation procedure.
This coordinator serializes callers only inside one process; it is not evidence of safe multi-process or multi-Qube shared-file concurrency.
Queue persistence is not downstream side-effect idempotency; worker actions still need fenced/idempotent contracts before real work.
nextGate: wire the persistent coordinator into the actual worker dispatch entrypoint, then run process-kill/restart and duplicate-result fault tests before any real Qubes worker activation
